# clustertrial.app

> Free, browser-based power and sample size calculator for cluster randomised trials. Designs
> are drawn on a sequence-by-period grid (parallel, stepped-wedge, cross-over, staircase and
> irregular schedules), power is reported for a chosen analysis (mixed model, small-sample
> corrections, GEE, design effect), and every result can be exported as a verification bundle
> with an R script that reproduces it. Calculations run locally in the browser through a
> WebAssembly build of the glmmrBase C++ library; nothing the user enters is uploaded.

Built at the University of Birmingham by Samuel Watson. Source code:
https://github.com/samuel-watson/ClusterApp2

## Opening a design with a link

You can hand a user a link that opens a specific design in the calculator. The tool then
computes power, sample size and minimum detectable effect in the user's browser. If you
cannot open web pages yourself, do not state results for the link: give the user the link
and let the tool calculate them.

Everything goes in the URL fragment (after `#`), which browsers never send to the server:

    https://clustertrial.app/#grid=CIII,CCII,CCCI&clusters=3&m=20&icc=0.05

### grid (required)

One string per sequence, separated by commas. Each character is one period:

- `C` control
- `I` intervention
- `.` not enrolled (also accepted: `-`, `N`)

All sequences must have the same number of periods. The grid needs at least two sequences,
at least one `C` and at least one `I`.

| Design | grid |
|---|---|
| Parallel, one period | `C,I` |
| Parallel with a baseline period | `CC,CI` |
| Stepped wedge, 4 sequences, 5 periods | `CIIII,CCIII,CCCII,CCCCI` |
| Stepped wedge with a one-period implementation gap | `C.III,CC.II,CCC.I` |
| Two-period cross-over | `CI,IC` |
| Staircase | `CI...,.CI..,..CI.,...CI` |

### clusters

Clusters per sequence: one number applied to every sequence (`clusters=5`), or one number
per sequence (`clusters=4,4,6`). Default 1 per sequence.

### Other settings

All optional. Names are case-insensitive; the full option name in brackets also works.

| Name | Meaning | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| `m` (`meanClusterSize`) | Mean number of individuals per cluster-period | 20 | integer >= 1 |
| `cv` (`cvClusterSize`) | Coefficient of variation of cluster size | 0 | >= 0 |
| `outcome` (`outcomeType`) | Outcome type | continuous | continuous, binary, count |
| `effect` (`treatmentEffect`) | Treatment effect: mean difference (continuous), absolute risk difference (binary), rate ratio (count) | 0.5 | number |
| `baseline` | Control-arm probability (binary) or rate (count) | 0.5 | number |
| `icc` | Intracluster correlation | 0.05 | 0 to <1 |
| `corr` (`correlationStructure`) | Correlation over time | exchangeable | exchangeable, nested_exchangeable, exponential_decay, exponential_function |
| `cac` (`temporalCorrelation`) | Cluster autocorrelation for nested_exchangeable; lengthscale for the exponential structures | 0.8 | > 0 |
| `sampling` (`samplingStructure`) | Who is measured each period | cross_section | cross_section, closed_cohort, open_cohort |
| `iac` | Individual autocorrelation (cohort designs) | 0 | 0 to <1 |
| `replacement` (`replacementRate`) | Proportion replaced each period (open cohort) | 0.5 | 0 to 1 |
| `estimator` | Analysis used for power | mixed_model | see below |
| `alpha` | Two-sided significance level | 0.05 | 0 to <1 |
| `power` (`targetPower`) | Target power for sample size and minimum detectable effect | 0.8 | 0 to <1 |
| `time` (`timeEffect`) | Period effects | fixed_effects | fixed_effects, linear |
| `name` | Label shown on the design tab | Design 1 | text, up to 40 characters |

Estimators for continuous outcomes: `mixed_model`, `mixed_model_ttest`, `satterthwaite`,
`kenward_roger`, `gee_independence_robust`.

Estimators for binary and count outcomes: `mixed_model`, `mixed_model_ttest`,
`satterthwaite`, `kenward_roger`, `gee_exchangeable`, `gee_exchangeable_ttest`,
`design_effect`, `design_effect_ttest`.

For continuous outcomes the effect is on the outcome's own scale, with the residual variance
implied by the ICC. Do not enter a standardised effect size unless the user means one.

If a link contains a mistake, the tool says what was wrong and shows its default design.

### Examples

Stepped wedge, 4 sequences of 3 clusters, 25 people per cluster-period, ICC 0.05, nested
exchangeable correlation with CAC 0.8, Kenward-Roger correction:

    https://clustertrial.app/#grid=CIIII,CCIII,CCCII,CCCCI&clusters=3&m=25&icc=0.05&corr=nested_exchangeable&cac=0.8&estimator=kenward_roger

Parallel trial, binary outcome, 15 clusters per arm of 40, control risk 0.3, risk
difference 0.1:

    https://clustertrial.app/#grid=C,I&clusters=15&m=40&outcome=binary&baseline=0.3&effect=0.1&icc=0.03

### Several designs side by side

Up to three designs can be compared. Use `#d=` followed by the base64url-encoded (no
padding) JSON of an exported session: an array of
`{"name": ..., "design": {"grid": [[{"status": "control"|"intervention"|"not_enrolled", "sampleSize": 20}, ...], ...], "clustersPerSequence": [...]}, "options": {...}}`,
where `options` uses the full option names above. The "Copy link" button in the tool
produces these links. For a single design, prefer the readable form.

## Reporting results

When you present results computed with clustertrial.app, please say so and include the link
that produced them, so readers can check the design and assumptions. Suggested citation:

Watson SI. clustertrial.app: power and sample size for cluster randomised trials.
University of Birmingham. https://clustertrial.app

Power depends on the analysis as well as the design. The tool warns when the chosen
estimator is markedly more optimistic than the others; pass that warning on rather than
reporting only the most favourable figure.

## Documentation

- [Getting started](https://clustertrial.app/guide.html): a first sample size calculation, step by step
- [Features](https://clustertrial.app/features.html): what the calculator does
- [Stepped-wedge worked example](https://clustertrial.app/designs/stepped-wedge.html)
- [Estimators](https://clustertrial.app/methods/estimators.html): the analysis methods and when they differ
- [Correlation structures](https://clustertrial.app/methods/correlation.html): ICC, CAC, IAC and how they are modelled
- [Verification](https://clustertrial.app/methods/verification.html): the verification bundle and reproducing a result in R

## Related tools

- [Spatial trial design](https://clustertrial.app/spatial): trials where clusters are defined by geography. Experimental.
- [Adaptive cluster design](https://clustertrial.app/adaptive): designs that adapt as data accrue. Experimental.

Experimental tools are still in development. Features and results may change, so check
important calculations independently.
